messages:
Sam (CS): heads up — Acme onboarding hit 403s on generate calls. They say embeddings worked fine. Escalating for quick triage.
Acme Oncall: repro steps below. Tried from our app and curl. embedding calls succeed but generate returns 403.
Acme Oncall: ```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-onboard-abc123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```
Acme Oncall: response: ```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient_scope",
    "message": "missing scope:inference.generate"
  }
}
```
Maria (Eng): thanks Sam. @Acme Oncall — quick question: was that API key created via the dashboard "Create token" flow after SSO login, or via our tokens API/CLI?
Acme Oncall: created from the org console after SSO sign-in. We didn't use CLI.
Jordan (ProdOps): pulling audit — token sk-acme-onboard-abc123 was issued by tokens.create (UI) at 2025-10-01T12:02:10Z, scopes: ["embeddings.create","usage.read"]. Looks like inference.generate is indeed missing.
Kevin (AuthBot): policy check: org-level SSO token provisioning policy for Acme forbids granting inference scopes to tokens created by non-admin SSO users. (rule: allow_inference_scopes=false).
Amy (Support): ok that matches the 403. Two paths to fix: 1) Admin enables inference scope for SSO-created tokens in console or 2) create a dedicated API token via the tokens API/CLI with explicit scopes. Recommend option 2 for fastest unblock.
Amy (Support): example (CLI):
```
redwood tokens create --name "acme-onboard-inference" --scopes inference.generate,embeddings.create
# returns: sk-new-xxxx
```
Amy (Support): or via API (admin):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-<org-admin-key>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"name":"acme-onboard-inference","scopes":["inference.generate","embeddings.create"]}'
```
Maria (Eng): note for engineering — if customer must keep SSO token workflow, Product can add a clearer warning in the UI when creating tokens under SSO-restricted orgs (we already show a tooltip but it's not prominent). Also logging could include the missing scope string in the 403 body (we already do, but double-check).
Jordan (ProdOps): security note: if you patch an existing key to add inference, ensure rotation: do not reuse the same token in prod until you've validated. Recommend create-new-and-rotate.
Sam (CS): passing to customer with suggested commands + admin note. Also cc @security for org policy followup.
Acme Oncall: created new token via CLI as suggested and it worked. Here's the working curl:```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-new-xxxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Acme Oncall: response: 200 with text stream. :white_check_mark:
Amy (Support): great — marking as resolved. For the record I created a follow-up ticket to update the dashboard copy for SSO-limited orgs (TICKET-4532).
Maria (Eng): also added a small telemetry flag to flag UI token creates that omit inference scopes so we can measure how often this trips people.
Sam (CS): thanks everyone — closing the loop with Acme and including steps in onboarding checklist (create API token with inference scope OR request admin enable).
Acme Oncall: thanks all! very fast turnaround.
